newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki bourse may start trade in euros from '99.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki bourse may start trade in euros from '99.

text.p: All securities listed on the Helsinki stock exchange will be denominated in euros from the start of 1999 if Finland joins EMU, the finance ministry said with the publication of its EMU changeover plan on Wednesday.

"The Helsinki stock exchange will start trading in euros right at the beginning of the third stage of economic and monetary union (EMU)," Rauno Niinimaki, head of the ministry's EMU project told a news conference.
"This will include all the securities traded: shares, options, subscriptions rights and bonds," he said, adding the switch to euro from markka was up to whether Finland joined EMU.
The whole chain of bourse trade, which includes dealing, clearing and custody will be conducted in euros from the start of the third stage of EMU, the report said.
Central government funding and cash asset investments will also be converted into euros at the start of monetary union on condition that Finland joins in the first wave.
New government bonds will be issued in euros from the start of the 1999-2002 transition period, Niinimaki said.
But the question of converting existing government bonds to euros was still open, he said, adding that it would be "preferable" to have old bonds converted into euros as soon as possible.
"We are currently investigating the practical obstacles in that matter," Niinimaki said.
The fate of the state's foreign currency debt was also still open.

"The latest sentiment seems to be that if Finland has foreign currency debt in another euro-country's currency, for example in German marks, that debt can be converted to euros after Germany converts its own mark debt to euros," Niinimaki said.
Other open questions included the question how the Bank of Finland's reference rates, such as the Helibor interest rates, could be converted to euro, he said.
The Bank of Finland will eventually end the quotation of the base rate, Helibor rates and the quotation of its three- and five-year reference rates during the transition period.
The EMU changeover plan published today was a first version and will be updated every six months, the finance ministry said.
